## Overview

This course introduces graduate students to the theory and application of quantitative methods in political science. We cover the foundations of statistical inference, linear regression, maximum likelihood estimation, and model diagnostics using R. The goal is for students to leave the course able to conduct, interpret, and present original quantitative research.

All computing is done in [R](https://www.r-project.org/) using the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) and [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/). We use [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) for reproducible documents.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. Formulate testable hypotheses from political science theories
2. Manage, clean, and visualize data using R and the tidyverse
3. Estimate and interpret linear regression models
4. Assess model fit and diagnose violations of assumptions
5. Present statistical results in publication-ready tables and figures
6. Produce reproducible research documents with Quarto

## Software

We use R exclusively in this course. Install the following before the first class:

- [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) (latest version)
- [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/)
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)

Key packages:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "modelsummary", "fixest",
  "marginaleffects", "ggplot2", "here",
  "quarto", "tinytable"
))
```
